classification: primary-documentation-only; these excerpts are not native observations

claims: EBS direct permissions may grant snapshot access to a caller denied EC2 CopySnapshot or CreateVolume access.
Tagging through StartSnapshot uses ec2:CreateTags authorization as well as EBS permissions.

Customer-managed KMS keys require permission through key policies/IAM; the guide recommends conditioning CreateGrant with kms:GrantIsForAWSResource. This recommendation alone is not proof that each EBS direct operation invokes CreateGrant.
ParentSnapshotId with any explicit Encrypted or KmsKeyArn rejects with ValidationException.
With encryption fields omitted, encrypted children inherit the encrypted parent's KMS key.

With encryption-by-default disabled, an unencrypted parent produces an unencrypted child; encryption-by-default enabled rejects an unencrypted parent. The enabled-default case is not probed because account defaults must remain unchanged.
An encrypted parent requires permission to use its KMS key.
StartSnapshot creates a pending snapshot; PutSnapshotBlock supplies data.
Reading an encrypted snapshot block requires permission to use its KMS key.

The ViaService support table lists Amazon EBS as ec2.${AWS_region}.amazonaws.com (EBS only), and the AWS-managed EBS key example uses ec2.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. Native EBS direct API ViaService values are established separately by conditioned calls, not inferred from this example or event invokedBy.
kms:EncryptionContext:context-key can constrain symmetric cryptographic requests by context key and value; it is a single-valued condition key.

Disabling a KMS key prevents cryptographic operations subject to eventual consistency; data-key use can continue until the KMS key is needed again. The page's EC2 volume attachment example does not establish EBS direct API caching or lifetime.
Customer-managed key deletion requires a 7–30 day waiting period; PendingDeletion is not immediate physical deletion.
